messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Extracting sigma hat
parts:
My turn to ask a stupid question.
--what is the simple way to extract the model-implied covariance matrix as a symmetric matrix?

I am trying to extract the model-implied covariance matrix as a matrix, so that I can use it in matrix calculations. I run an analysis:

out.BB.lavaan<-sem(model=model_Bergami_Bagozzi,data=BergamiBagozzi2000,
                   auto.fix.first=F,std.lv=T,std.ov=T)

and extract the fitted covariance matrix:

BB.sigma<-lavTech(out.BB.lavaan,"fitted")

and then examine this object:

str(BB.sigma)

and am told:

List of 1
 $ :List of 1
  ..$ cov: num [1:20, 1:20] 0.997 0.589 0.541 0.577 0.577 ...

I have tried using matrix()  and as.matrix() to turn this into a matrix, but it keeps being a list.

I tried to use the result in a matrix function and got the most peculiar error message:

Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'a' in selecting a method for function 'solve': error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'Schur': internal problem in as(): “lavaan.matrix.symmetric” is(object, "matrix") is TRUE, but the metadata asserts that the 'is' relation is FALSE

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 303bc0a2000dd08a
messages.subject: Re: Extracting sigma hat
parts:
I think you should be able to export the covariance matrix in the list element with this. The covariance matrix is just stored as the first element in the list which you can store in a new object.

BB.sigma.matrix <- BB.sigma[[1]][[1]]

Drew

Andrew M. Engelhardt
(he/him/his)
Assistant Professor 
Department of Political Science
University of North Carolina, Greensboro

Thanks! This code:

BB.sigma<-lavTech(out.BB.lavaan,"fitted")
BB.sigma.matrix<-matrix(BB.sigma[[1]][[1]],nrow=20,byrow=T)

produced a BB.sigma.matrix that R is happy with.

I've got another error message, but it isn't related to lavaan.

Thanks again!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Extracting sigma hat
parts:
On 8/16/21 10:04 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> My turn to ask a stupid question.
> --what is the simple way to extract the model-implied covariance matrix
> as a symmetric matrix?

The standard way is this:

SigmaHat <- lavInspect(fit, "implied")$cov
SigmaHat

You can also use "fitted" instead of "implied".

If you 'print' the matrix, you will only see the lower half, and three
digits after the decimal point. But that is just for pretty printing.
For further calculations, R uses the full matrix.

If you don't want the pretty printing, you can use

SigmaHat <- lavInspect(fit, "implied", add.class = FALSE)$cov
SigmaHat

Yves.
